overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating via email among a quorum on May 13 and May 16; emergency question not reached. Ordered email release and future compliance.

allegations.summary: Board member emailed all members on May 13 about an outdoor Town Meeting or masks, and three members replied to the whole Board by email.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the emails contain improper deliberations because these emails reached a quorum of the Board and included members’ opinions on matters within the Board’s jurisdiction.

allegations.summary: Board member replied-all on May 16 to a staff email, giving an opinion on the length of a vendor permit suspension for tobacco sales to minors.
allegations.key_passage: The expression of an opinion of by one public body member on matters within the body’s jurisdiction to a quorum of a public body is a deliberation, even if no other public body member responds.

allegations.summary: Board argued the May 13 mask discussion was an emergency that did not require notice; the AG did not decide whether an emergency existed.
allegations.key_passage: Regardless, because the discussions took place via email outside of a posted meeting, the Board violated the Open Meeting Law, and we need not reach the question of whether the circumstances here constituted an emergency.

remedy: Publicly release the May 13 and May 16 emails within 30 days of receipt of the determination, to the extent not already done.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
remedy_passage: In addition, we order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
